newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine austerity measures pass budget committee.
newsitem.headline: Argentine austerity measures pass budget committee.

text.p: The budget and finance committee of Argentina's lower house of Congress gave its approval Wednesday to the government's austerity measures and passed them on for debate in the Chamber of Deputies.
"There was a favorable decision by the Peronist majority in the committee," committee president Oscar Lamberto of the ruling Peronist party told reporters.
The Peronist lawmakers approved the increase in VAT to a set of services with only minor changes, and the hike in the price of gasoline, the package's two biggest revenue-boosting measures.

But it decided to maintain the system by which income from gasoline is distributed proportionally among the provinces and central administration, opposing the government proposal to allow for a larger share of revenue to go to central coffers.
Economy Minister Roque Fernndez announced the belt-tightening measures three weeks ago in an effort to reduce the country's fiscal gap.
The Chamber of Deputies should begin discussing the austerity package in seven to 15 days, said Lamberto.
He said the measures will be examined simultaneously in the Senate.
Analysts said the measures could be passed sometime in September.
